title: Daily Conversation
subtitle: Introduce yourself and get by
description: The handful of phrases you'll repeat constantly when meeting new people — your PG owner, your auto driver, your neighbor.

items.context: The simplest introduction — fill in the blank with your name. Locals will immediately feel a connection when you say this in Kannada
items.scenario: Introducing yourself to your PG owner, a new colleague, or anyone asking who you are

items.context: Formal way to ask someone's name — nimma is respectful, use it with elders and people you've just met
items.scenario: Meeting your landlord for the first time, or asking the name of a shopkeeper you visit regularly

items.context: Say this when you're struggling and need to switch — most educated Bengalureans are comfortable in English and will happily switch
items.scenario: When a conversation gets too complex, or you're stuck in an important situation like a government office

items.context: This phrase is a cheat code — locals light up when they hear it. It breaks down barriers faster than anything else you can say
items.scenario: When someone is surprised you're speaking Kannada, or to warm up a conversation with anyone local

items.context: Nobody speaks textbook Kannada in real life — this gives you a fighting chance to actually understand the reply
items.scenario: Whenever someone responds too fast in rapid Bengaluru Kannada and you've completely lost the thread

items.context: Be honest — pretending you understood when you didn't leads to real problems, especially with addresses and prices
items.scenario: When you genuinely didn't catch what was said and need them to try again or differently

items.context: Short, simple, universally understood — matte means again, hēḷi means tell/say
items.scenario: When you missed what was said — auto drivers, phone calls, or any noisy street conversation

items.context: Fill in your home city or state — inda means from. This always sparks a warm conversation about where you're from
items.scenario: When new people ask about you — PG residents, classmates, or anyone curious about the outsider speaking Kannada

items.context: Shows interest in the other person — Kannadigas are proud of their roots and love talking about their district or native place
items.scenario: Getting to know your auto driver, a shopkeeper, or any local you've started chatting with

items.context: Kannadigas are family-oriented — asking about someone's family is a sign of genuine warmth and will make them feel respected
items.scenario: In ongoing relationships — your regular vegetable vendor, the chai uncle near your college, or a helpful neighbour
